text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Serbian parliament speaker called an extraordinary session next Tuesday. Draft laws on recognisiton of part of local election results according to OSCE recommendations and on election of government members.
- Serb regional assembly in Eastern Slavonia and West Srem in Croatia appealed on Serbs to remain in the region and asked for postponment of local elections scheduled for March 16.
- About 3,000 Serbs of Vukovar in Eastern Slavonia in Croatia held a protest meeting on Wednesday demanding local elections to be postponed and integritiy of the region even after elections.
- Serbian chamber of commerce said on Wednesday insolvency and administration slow down development of entrepreneurship.
- About three billion dinars ($555 million) needed for spring campaign, Serbian chamber of commerce said.
- Serbian oppositon leaders, invited by the French Foreign Minister Hervet de Charette, leave for Paris on Thursday.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian teachers, on strike since January 15, received on Wednesday only assurances from the republics government it was willing to find the solution to pay late wages.
- Serbian government is expected to cut number of ministers from 31 to 23 at its session on February 11, sources close to the government said.
BORBA
- Full support in the country and abroad for Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's initiative for resolving post-election crisis in Serbia.
- Socialist Party of Serbia main board says Milosevic's initiative will contribute to advancing relations between Yugoslavia and the OSCE and international community in general.
- Serb assembly of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and western Srem calls for postponement of elections.
- Trade unions and government begin talks over work stoppages in educational, scientific and cultural institutions in Serbia.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Opposition coalition Zajedno supporters protests continue in Belgrade. Belgrade lawyers join protest.
- Illegal Albanian terrorist organization "Liberation ARmy of Kosova" confirms three Albanians killed in attack on police patrol near Vucitrn were its members.
- Adriatic port of Bar plans transshipment of three million tonnes of cargo in 1997.
- Only a few banks can set aside funds for credits. Outstanding debts "freeze" funds for new credits.

- Serbia needs $560 million to import 2.6 million tonnes of crude oil and 561,000 tonnes of derivatives this year, imports of oil derivatives to be halved compared to 1996, says Dragan Tomic, director of Jugopetrol.
